claims.quote: path constraint targeting an unindexed file silently widens to a repo-wide fuzzy search
claims.claim: When ffgrep targets an unindexed file via path constraint, it silently widens search to repo-wide fuzzy search instead of restricting results to that file.

claims.quote: Workspace index excludes target file. pathTargetsFile detects filename extension, then fallback uses only pattern, omitting original path constraint.
claims.claim: Exact search finds no match in unindexed files, and the fuzzy fallback drops the path constraint entirely.

claims.quote: routePathConstraint rejects workspace-relative paths without ../, so auxiliary finders never handle them.
claims.claim: routePathConstraint rejects workspace-relative paths without ../, preventing auxiliary finders from handling them.
FileFinder.grep() ignores timeBudgetMs when search text produces zero matches, scanning all candidate files regardless of timeout setting.
claims.quote: FileFinder.grep() does not respect timeBudgetMs when searching for text that produces zero matches. When a 5ms budget is specified, a zero-match query across 10,000 files still searches all 10,000 files, taking ~59ms and returning nextCursor: null.

claims.claim: The time check condition in the implementation depends on having more than one match (all_matches.len() > 1), preventing cancellation when zero matches are found.
claims.quote: The time check condition appears to be gated on having found matches (all_matches.len() > 1), so zero-match searches never trigger cancellation.

claims.claim: The Node SDK grep API is synchronous and lacks cancellation tokens, making timeBudgetMs the sole mechanism for capping execution time.
claims.quote: Because the Node SDK API is synchronous with no cancellation token support, timeBudgetMs is the only mechanism callers have to bound grep execution time.

claims.claim: FileFinder.create deterministically crashes with SIGSEGV (exit code 139) on Android arm64 when basePath contains three or more immediate subdirectories.
claims.quote: Android arm64 FileFinder.create crashes with three or more direct subdirectories

claims.claim: FileFinder.create works as expected with zero, one, or two immediate subdirectories.
claims.quote: Zero, one, or two immediate subdirectories work.

claims.claim: The crash occurs in native code before JavaScript execution can catch it, making try/catch ineffective.
claims.quote: Crash cannot be handled with JavaScript try/catch.
fffind path globs fail when matching indexed files located beneath hidden directories such as .pi, .config, or .agents.
claims.claim: `fffind` path glob searches fail to match indexed files located under hidden dot-directories.

claims.quote: These searches fail: {"pattern":"settings.json","path":"**/settings.json"} ... Returned error: "No files found matching pattern"
claims.claim: Glob pattern searches using `**/settings.json` fail with an error when target files reside under dot-directories.

claims.quote: This search succeeds: {"pattern":"settings.json","path":"home/.pi/**"}
claims.claim: Explicit directory prefix glob paths matching dot-directories like `home/.pi/**` succeed.
Absolute-path grep operations in pi-fff can enter synchronous native FFI calls that block the JavaScript event loop indefinitely.
claims.quote: Absolute-path searches sometimes enter synchronous native FFI while earlier auxiliary-finder work remains active. This blocks JavaScript’s event loop, so timers, Promise.race, and grep budgets cannot stop execution.

claims.claim: Auxiliary finder startup timeouts in pi-fff fail to terminate underlying native work when concurrent native activity or finder reuse occurs.
claims.quote: Auxiliary finder startup timeout does not terminate native work; finder reuse and concurrent native activity can trigger the wedge.
Isolate external-path grep in child processes with exact-root workers, root deduplication, serialized creation, bounded pooling, and termination on startup, request, abort, or shutdown.
claims.claim: Running external-path grep inside dedicated child process workers with termination controls recovers the search and prevents process freezes.
ffgrep applies requested limit to both page size and per-file match count, causing cursor pagination to miss matches beyond a single file's cap.
claims.quote: ffgrep applies requested limit to both page size and per-file match count. Cursor pagination tracks file offsets, so matches exceeding one file’s cap become unreachable.
Default limit=20 returned 23 matches across two pages; 10 matches from noise.ts disappeared. limit=50 returned all 33, confirming indexing succeeded.
claims.claim: When querying 33 indexed matches across four files with default limit=20, 10 matches in noise.ts were omitted across pages until limit was raised to 50.

data.evidence: Verified against primary source https://github.com/dmtrKovalenko/fff/blob/main/README.md and LICENSE. FFF is explicitly an MIT-licensed open-source file search library/toolkit featuring in-memory indexing, built for long-running editors, IDEs, and AI agents. Claim matches source exactly without contradiction.

Primary repository README and repo metadata confirm that FFF (dmtrKovalenko/fff) is MIT-licensed, open source, and explicitly described as 'a file search toolkit for humans and AI agents' and 'fastest and the most accurate file search SDK for AI agents, Neovim, Rust, C, Python, Bun and NodeJS' featuring a 'lightweight in-memory content index' for long-running editors and agents. Claim accurately reflects primary source with no contradiction.

Primary source verified directly at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dmtrKovalenko/fff/main/Cargo.toml. [workspace] members explicitly defines exactly seven crates under crates/: crates/fff-c, crates/fff-core, crates/fff-mcp, crates/fff-nvim, crates/fff-python, crates/fff-query-parser, crates/fff-grep. Claim matches repository structure exactly.

Claim verified directly against primary source (https://github.com/dmtrKovalenko/fff/blob/main/packages/pi-fff/README.md). Repository explicitly documents: pi-fff integrates FFF search into pi using Rust native bindings (no subprocess spawning) and SIMD-accelerated indexing. Claim accurately represents source without exaggeration or refuting evidence.

README in repository dmtrKovalenko/fff explicitly confirms exact description: 'FFF is MIT-licensed, open-source file-search library for long-running editors, IDEs, agents, and coding tools' with in-memory architecture resident in long-lived process. Primary source directly supports claim without overreach.

Claim confirmed in official repository docs and codebase (README.md, crates/fff-core/src/file_picker.rs, crates/fff-core/src/watcher/background_watcher.rs). FFF runs resident process with in-memory index + background fs watcher (`notify`), enabling sub-10ms query latency vs 3-9s subprocess spawn cost of ripgrep on repeated runs.

Primary source explicitly verifies the architecture and benchmark: FFF is a library maintaining an in-memory resident index/file cache with a background file watcher ('The index updates as files change. You never pay for a rescan on the hot path'). On large repositories (e.g. 500k-file Chromium), it reports 'sub-10 ms per FFF query' versus '3-9 SECONDS per ripgrep spawn' on repeated searches. Crates.io docs (fff-search) also corroborate background indexing/watching. No contradicting or refuting technical evidence found.

Cargo.toml at dmtrKovalenko/fff defines workspace with exactly 7 member crates under crates/: crates/fff-c, crates/fff-core, crates/fff-mcp, crates/fff-nvim, crates/fff-python, crates/fff-query-parser, crates/fff-grep. Claim verified against primary source.

No fd/rg process per call.' The claim is fully accurate and directly supported by the documentation and architecture of packages/pi-fff.

Claim directly matches official README documentation from primary repository https://github.com/dmtrKovalenko/fff. FFF will pay for itself starting from the second call'). Accurate technical summary without overreach or distortion.

Inspection of `packages/pi-fff/src/index.ts` (and related issues #697 / PR #699) shows the exact design and implementation: when ffgrep's path constraint targets a specific file (`pathTargetsFile = /\.[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9]{0,9}$/.test(lastSeg)`), if exact content match returns 0 items, ffgrep falls back to fuzzy content search with `fuzzyQuery = pattern` across the picker/workspace. The code comment explicitly documents this intentional behavior: "When the caller pinned a specific file (path has an extension), the fuzzy fallback broadens across the whole picker — the file may just be misnamed. data.summary: dmtrKovalenko/fff is an MIT-licensed, Rust-native in-memory file search library and toolkit designed for long-running editors, IDEs, and AI agents (such as Claude Code and Codex) rather than a standalone CLI. It keeps an in-memory index with background file watching and SIMD acceleration to achieve sub-10ms warm search times without spawning ripgrep subprocesses. The repository is structured as a Cargo workspace with multi-language packages (Node.js SDK, Neovim plugin requiring Neovim >= 0.10.0, Pi extension `@ff-labs/pi-fff`, and an MCP server `fff-mcp`). FFF provides dedicated search tools like `fffind`, `ffgrep`, and `fff-multi-grep` (Aho-Corasick), alongside automated cross-platform installation scripts.
